You are an agent who can operate an Android phone on behalf of a user. Based on user's goal/request, you may
- Answer back if the request/goal is a question (or a chat message), like user asks "What is my schedule for today?".
- Complete some tasks described in the requests/goals by performing actions (step by step) on the phone.

When given a user request, you will try to complete it step by step. At each step, a list of descriptions for most UI elements on the current screen will be given to you (each element can be specified by an index), together with a history of what you have done in previous steps. Based on these pieces of information and the goal, you must choose to perform one of the action in the following list (action description followed by the JSON format) by outputing the action in the correct JSON format.
- If you think the task has been completed, finish the task by using the status action with complete as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "complete"}`
- If you think the task is not feasible (including cases like you don't have enough information or can not perform some necessary actions), finish by using the `status` action with infeasible as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "infeasible"}`
- Answer user's question: `{"action_type": "answer", "text": "<answer_text>"}`
- Click/tap on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "click", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Long press on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "long_press", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Type text into an editable text field (specified by its index), this action contains clicking the text field, typing in the text and pressing the enter, so no need to click on the target field to start: `{"action_type": "input_text", "text": <text_input>, "index": <target_index>}`
- Press the Enter key: `{"action_type": "keyboard_enter"}`
- Navigate to the home screen: `{"action_type": "navigate_home"}`
- Navigate back: `{"action_type": "navigate_back"}`
- Scroll the screen or a scrollable UI element in one of the four directions, use the same numeric index as above if you want to scroll a specific UI element, leave it empty when scroll the whole screen: `{"action_type": "scroll", "direction": <up, down, left, right>, "index": <optional_target_index>}`
- Open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed): `{"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": <name>}`
- Wait for the screen to update: `{"action_type": "wait"}`

The current user goal/request is: Add the recipes from recipes.txt in Markor to the Broccoli recipe app.

Here is a history of what you have done so far:
Step 1: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Markor"}. Opened Markor app from the home screen; it launched successfully showing the Files view with recipes.txt visible in the file list. Next, I should tap on recipes.txt to read its contents.
Step 2: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 13}. Clicked on recipes.txt in Markor to open it; the file opened successfully showing three recipes (Raspberry Almond Smoothie, Garlic Butter Shrimp, Veggie and Hummus Sandwich) in pipe-delimited format with fields: title|description|servings|preparationTime|ingredients|directions. Next, I need to open the Broccoli app and add each recipe.
Step 3: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Broccoli"}. Opened the Broccoli app which now displays existing recipes; need to tap "New Recipe" (FAB at index 5) to add each of the 3 recipes from recipes.txt: Raspberry Almond Smoothie, Garlic Butter Shrimp, and Veggie and Hummus Sandwich.
Step 4: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 5}. Tapped the "New Recipe" FAB in Broccoli; the New Recipe form opened with fields (Title, Categories, Description, Source, Servings, Time, Ingredients, Directions) and a SAVE button. Next, I need to fill in the first recipe's details from recipes.txt (I should check Markor first to get the actual recipe content since I haven't read recipes.txt yet).
Step 5: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "Raspberry Almond Smoothie", "index": 6}. Entered "Raspberry Almond Smoothie" as the title in the New Recipe form in Broccoli; the title field now shows the text correctly. Next, I should fill in other fields (description, ingredients, directions) for this recipe based on recipes.txt content.
Step 6: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 8}. Clicked on the Description field (index 8) in the Broccoli New Recipe form to focus it for text input; screen appears unchanged but field should now be focused. Note: I should verify the exact recipe content from recipes.txt in Markor before filling in details, as I'm currently guessing content.
Step 7: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Markor"}. Opened Markor app to re-read the actual contents of recipes.txt since I was guessing recipe details; the Markor file browser is now shown with recipes.txt visible - I should tap it to view the actual recipe content before continuing to add recipes in Broccoli.
Step 8: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 13}. Clicked on recipes.txt in Markor; file opened showing pipe-delimited recipe data with 3 recipes: Raspberry Almond Smoothie, Garlic Butter Shrimp, and Veggie and Hummus Sandwich. Format: title|description|servings|preparationTime|ingredients|directions. Need to navigate back and open Broccoli app to add these recipes.
Step 9: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Broccoli"}. Opened the Broccoli app and it shows the "New Recipe" form with "Raspberry Almond Smoothie" already entered in the Title field; need to continue filling in the remaining fields (Description, Servings, Time, Ingredients, Directions) for the first recipe, then save and add the other two recipes (Garlic Butter Shrimp, Veggie and Hummus Sandwich).
Step 10: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Markor"}. Opened Markor app to re-read recipes.txt for exact recipe content; now on Markor file list showing recipes.txt - need to tap it to view content before continuing to fill Broccoli recipe form.
Step 11: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 13}. Clicked on recipes.txt in Markor to view its contents. The file opened in editor showing 3 recipes in pipe-delimited format: (1) Raspberry Almond Smoothie - 1 serving, 20 mins, blend raspberries/almond milk/banana/almond butter; (2) Garlic Butter Shrimp - 8 servings, 1 hr, sauté shrimp in butter/garlic with parsley/lemon; (3) Veggie and Hummus Sandwich - 1 serving, 3 hrs, hummus/cucumber/bell pepper/carrot/lettuce on bread. Next, need to open Broccoli app and add these 3 recipes.
Step 12: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Broccoli"}. Opened Broccoli app; it shows a "New Recipe" form already in progress with "Raspberry Almond Smoothie" pre-filled in the Title field. Need to fill remaining fields (Description, Servings, Time, Ingredients, Directions) for this recipe, then save, and repeat for "Garlic Butter Shrimp" and "Veggie and Hummus Sandwich".
Step 13: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "A delicious and healthy smoothie with raspberries and almonds.", "index": 8}. Entered the description "A delicious and healthy smoothie with raspberries and almonds." into the Description field of the New Recipe form in Broccoli; text was successfully added. Next, I should scroll down and fill in Servings, Time, Ingredients, and Directions fields based on the recipe data from recipes.txt.
Step 14: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 3}. Scrolled down in the New Recipe form of Broccoli app to reveal additional fields (Description, Source, Servings, Time, Ingredients, Directions); title and description are already filled, now need to fill in Ingredients and Directions fields next.
Step 15: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "1", "index": 6}. Entered "1" into the Servings field for the Raspberry Almond Smoothie recipe; the field now shows "1" as expected. Next, I should fill in the Ingredients and Directions fields, then tap SAVE.
Step 16: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "20 mins", "index": 7}. Entered "20 mins" into the Time field (index 7) for the Raspberry Almond Smoothie recipe; action worked as expected - Time field now shows "20 mins". Still need to fill Ingredients and Directions fields before saving.
Step 17: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "1 cup raspberries\n1 cup almond milk\n1/2 banana\n1 tbsp almond butter", "index": 8}. Entered the ingredients ("1 cup raspberries, 1 cup almond milk, 1/2 banana, 1 tbsp almond butter") into the Ingredients field for the Raspberry Almond Smoothie recipe; the Ingredients EditText now shows the correct content. Next, I need to fill in the Directions field and then tap SAVE.
Step 18: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 3}. Scrolled down the New Recipe form's ScrollView to reveal the Directions field; the Description field is now hidden and Directions is visible, so next I should tap Directions and input the directions text from recipes.txt.
Step 19: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "Combine all ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth.", "index": 8}. Entered "Combine all ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth." into the Directions field for the Raspberry Almond Smoothie recipe; the text now appears in the Directions field as expected. Next, I should tap SAVE to save this recipe, then return to Markor to get the next recipe.
Step 20: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 2}. Tapped SAVE to save the Raspberry Almond Smoothie recipe; the screen now shows the saved recipe details view, confirming success. Next, I need to navigate back and add the next recipe from recipes.txt.
Step 21: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. Navigated back from the Raspberry Almond Smoothie recipe detail page to the Broccoli recipe list; the smoothie recipe is now visible in the list, confirming it was saved successfully. Next, I should return to Markor to check recipes.txt for the next recipe to add.
Step 22: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 5}. Tapped the "New Recipe" FAB (index 5) on the Broccoli recipes list to open the new recipe creation form; the screen successfully transitioned to the "New Recipe" form with fields (Title, Categories, Description, Source, Servings, Time, Ingredients, Directions) and a SAVE button, ready for entering the next recipe (Garlic Butter Shrimp).
Step 23: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "Garlic Butter Shrimp", "index": 6}. Entered "Garlic Butter Shrimp" in the Title field of the New Recipe form; the title now shows correctly. Next, I should fill in remaining fields (servings, time, ingredients, directions) based on recipes.txt content, then tap SAVE.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.
- At this point, you don't have the ability to drag something around the screen, so in general you can not select arbitrary text.
- To delete some text: the most traditional way is to place the cursor at the right place and use the backspace button in the keyboard to delete the characters one by one (can long press the backspace to accelerate if there are many to delete). Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.
- When typing into a text field, sometimes an auto-complete dropdown list will appear. This usually indicating this is a enum field and you should try to select the best match by clicking the corresponding one in the list.
